question: The part of an electric motor that reverses the direction of flow of current in it, is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**split ring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **split ring** is an essential component of a direct current (DC) motor, playing a key role in reversing the direction of current flow in the motor's coil.
 
• This reversal of current ensures that the motor's armature continues to rotate in a single direction by maintaining the torque acting on it.
 
• The split ring is connected to the external circuit via **carbon brushes**, allowing the motor to function smoothly.
 
• When the armature rotates, the split ring alternates the current direction every half-turn, ensuring continuous and uniform rotation of the motor's coil.
 
• This design is a critical feature of DC motors and is not typically found in alternating current (AC) motors, which use slip rings instead.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brushes in Electric Motors:**

 
 
• Brushes are typically made of carbon and are used to transfer current between the stationary parts of the motor and the rotating armature.
 
• They maintain contact with the split ring to ensure a continuous flow of current.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between Split Rings and Slip Rings:**
 
 
• Split rings are used in DC motors to reverse current direction, while slip rings are used in AC motors to transfer current without reversing it.
 
• Slip rings are continuous rings, whereas split rings are divided into two or more parts.
 
 
 
• **Armature in Electric Motors:**
 
 
• The armature is the rotating part of the motor where the current flows, creating a magnetic field that interacts with the external magnetic field.
 
• This interaction generates torque, causing the armature to rotate.
 
 
 
• **Working Principle of Electric Motors:**
 
 
• Electric motors work on the principle of electromagnetic induction, where a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a force.
 
• This force causes the conductor (armature) to rotate, converting electrical energy into mechanical energy.
